answers_to_key_questions.q1_slowest_experiments_why: All five slowest experiments are structural carryovers from unguarded historical queues, not research-duration outliers. Exp 786 (77 min): a resolved OOM investigation for RETRO-028, which was CLOSED in .62 — this experiment has zero research value in .63 and ran purely because the manifest check is missing at non-conductor dequeue sites. Exp 527 (52 min): a retired experiment (retired in .57) running for the 10th+ consecutive post-retirement appearance. Exp 491 (52 min): a JEPA diagnostic whose root cause (CPMI wiring miss) was identified externally, making the diagnostic's hypothesis potentially obsolete. Exp 627 (51 min): per-sentence verifier calls that paragraph-batching would reduce by 70% (recommended five consecutive milestones). Exp 603 (44 min): productive research that DualGPU migration would cut by 45% (recommended four consecutive milestones). The slowest experiments are not slow because they are complex — they are slow because mitigation governance is absent.
answers_to_key_questions.q2_gpu_utilization: Improved but structurally insufficient. GPU thermal differential at close = 0C (both 48C) vs .62's 9C — most balanced in project history. This likely reflects increased GPU 1 usage following RETRO-028 closure. However, both GPUs closed at 4MB/0% utilization, indicating sequential rather than parallel execution for the vast majority of experiments. DualGPU ThreadPoolExecutor validated at 1.8319x speedup (Exp 746, .57) remains unapplied for Exp 603/491-class across six consecutive milestones. The GPU utilization pattern is: full load during model inference, 0% between experiments, no concurrent training+inference pipeline.
answers_to_key_questions.q3_zombie_processes: None detected. GPU Zombie Killer (Exp 780) is working correctly. Both GPUs at 4MB/0% at close — driver-level context allocations only, no zombie processes. This is a CLEAN close. The 4MB allocation on each GPU is the nvidia driver context overhead, not process leakage. GPU close has been clean for multiple consecutive milestones since the Zombie Killer was deployed. RETRO-028 closure (Exp 810, .62) ensures Gemma4 no longer leaks VRAM between experiments.
answers_to_key_questions.q4_parallelization_opportunities: High-value parallelization opportunities exist and remain unexploited. (1) DualGPU: GPU 0 (Qwen inference) + GPU 1 (training or Gemma inference) simultaneously via ThreadPoolExecutor — validated at 1.8319x speedup, not applied to Exp 603/491-class. (2) CPU+GPU parallel: CPU-bound experiments (spec coverage check, type-check, constraint mining) can run concurrently with GPU inference during model load time. (3) Pre-flight test parallelization: the test suite runs sequentially against 728 experiments — pytest-xdist parallel execution would reduce pre-flight time. GPU monitor suggestion confirms: 'Both GPUs are idle. Use DualGPURunner to run Qwen on GPU 0 and Gemma on GPU 1 simultaneously.'
answers_to_key_questions.q5_preflight_bottleneck: Yes — and growing. The pre-flight test suite scales with experiment count: at 728 experiments, the test suite represents a significant fraction of wall time (estimated 14-15% at current scale, consistent with .54's 14.6% observation). Incremental test selection (Preflight v7, Exp 728-class) reduces this for the conductor-managed cycle, but the full-milestone pre-flight runs against the entire experiment corpus. Pytest-xdist parallel execution (using both CPUs and potentially GPU-agnostic tests on both GPUs simultaneously) is the highest-leverage pre-flight optimization. Target: reduce from ~728 min at 1 min/test to ~200 min with 4x parallelization.
answers_to_key_questions.q6_doc_reconciliation_efficiency: Efficient in the conductor cycle; not a bottleneck. Planning sessions (arxiv scan + experiment design + roadmap writing) are high-value and complete in ~1-2 hours per milestone. Conductor cycle doc updates (changelog + spec reconciliation) are lightweight and take <15 minutes per experiment. The inefficiency is in the implementation gap between retro documentation and operational action — the documentation itself is fast and accurate, but produces zero change. The retro process is not slow; it is disconnected from execution.
answers_to_key_questions.q7_tooling_infrastructure_changes: Seven changes would have the largest impact on .64 and beyond: (1) MILESTONE_PREREQS.md hard-blocking gate — prevents experiments from running until IMMEDIATE actions are signed off; (2) Manifest enforcement at ALL dequeue sites — eliminates Exp 527 (52 min) and Exp 786 (77 min) immediately; (3) ExperimentTimeoutWatchdog mandatory deployment — caps any unbounded experiment at 30 min with checkpoint saves; (4) RETRO-SYMCODE-SERIAL hard gate — escalates Exp 627 batching from recommendation to blocking requirement; (5) DualGPURunner systematic migration for Exp 603/491-class — 45 min/milestone savings; (6) Mandatory retirement sweep (retire >= added) as Phase 0 prerequisite — prevents experiment count from growing past 700 cap; (7) Pytest-xdist for pre-flight test parallelization — reduces test suite time by 4x.
